events.ai_basis: Trust region policy optimization (TRPO) performs consistently well for a wide range of crossing numbers

events.credibility_reason: Announcement only; no written argument until 2026, and the 2026 write-up does not state the quasi-polynomial bound; running-time form varies across talks.

Self-published Zenodo upload claiming a landmark polynomial algorithm via an unconventional 'resonance operator'; no expert uptake in ~17 months; later sources (Wikipedia, Lackenby 2026) still treat the problem as open; numerical validation only and reused constants per snippet; record itself unreadable.

events.ai_basis: We have developed a reinforcement learning agent that often finds a minimal sequence of unknotting crossing changes
We train neural agents that, when run from a given diagram, reliably find simplification trajectories.

why: The statement asks only whether unknot recognition is in P. Decidability, NP/coNP membership, exponential or empirical algorithms and Reidemeister-move bounds don't settle or bound that, so they get scope none. Unknotting-number work, torus-knot recognition and move-bounded untangling are different questions, so they're variant. The Lackenby 2026 paper gives a new decision algorithm but states no running time, so it moves nothing on the P question: none. The 2021 quasi-polynomial announcement is the one real bound on the running time. It is dated before the snapshot and is doubtful, because no argument was written down and the 2026 write-up omits the bound. The Zenodo polynomial claim would answer the whole question, but it shows several F10 signals together, so it is not_credible. AI roles: the RL agents in the 2024 and 2026 unknotting-number papers produced the unknotting sequences, so they are generated, but those events are variants. Gukov's TRPO certificates cover individual knots, so that event is instances.
doubts: The Zenodo record was never opened. It is judged only from a search snippet; if it were readable, the credibility call could change. It is also possible that arXiv:2607.23350 implicitly carries the quasi-polynomial bound. That is unverified, and the record says the text does not state it.
